items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: So Les went from hating the studio to falling in love with the studio, and then we made lots of great records because we had a way of capturing what it is that he did.

ctx.x: I think some artists may play a little different because they’re thinking this could be heard a lot. Someone could be listening to this.

The second you say we’re recording live — I made a lot of live records, most of them were not successful. When I say not successful, they didn’t become gigantic live recordings you know. Like Cannonball at the Jazz Workshop or Horace at the Village Gate or you know, Ramsey at the Bohemian Caverns, but when you get a live record that works, it works because you can’t get that in a studio. It only happens with the audience and the room and the weather and the night and whatever it is all kind of line up in the…
Well it’s really interesting too on the Joe Williams CD. You hear him talking to the audience and all that, and that’s great.
